title: Jana Nayagan Eyes Record Opening as Vijay's Final Film Sells 600,000 Advance Tickets
excerpt: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's farewell film opens July 23 across 8,000 screens in 30 countries, with trade analysts projecting a Rs 90 crore worldwide opening day.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jana Nayagan sold over 600,000 advance tickets, grossing Rs 15 crore domestically and Rs 27 crore globally.
  • Trade analysts project a Rs 90 crore global opening day and Rs 250 crore worldwide for the weekend.
  • The film opens on 8,000 screens across 30 countries, with 3,500 shows in Tamil Nadu alone.
  • Despite piracy leaks, demand is high, with theatres experiencing tremendous pressure for tickets.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's farewell film Jana Nayagan is on track for one of the biggest openings in Indian cinema, with advance bookings shattering records days before its July 23 theatrical release.

By Tuesday, July 21, over 600,000 tickets had been sold for opening day across India, according to industry tracker Sacnilk. The film had crossed Rs 15 crore in domestic advance bookings within 48 hours of ticket sales opening on July 19. Global pre-sales for the opening weekend have surpassed Rs 27 crore.

Trade Experts See Rs 90 Crore Worldwide Opening

Southern films trade analyst Ramesh Bala told NDTV he estimates a Rs 60 crore opening day in India and Rs 90 crore globally. For the opening weekend, Bala projected Rs 150–180 crore domestically and Rs 250 crore worldwide.

Trade expert Taran Adarsh declined to pin exact figures but predicted a "thunderous" opening, telling NDTV that "Vijay's popularity is at its peak" and advance bookings are "phenomenal." A source in the Theatre Owners Association told PTI there is even a possibility of the film entering the Rs 1,000 crore club.

Ticket Frenzy in Tamil Nadu

The demand in Tamil Nadu has been staggering. Within hours of pre-sales opening, single screens and multiplexes together sold over 90,000 tickets. Kamala Cinemas in Chennai moved 10,000 tickets within minutes of its portal going live. Mayajaal Multiplex sold out 48 shows in less than an hour.

"Vijay is no longer just a star — he's the Chief Minister. Fans are living a moment of their lives."

— Ramesh Bala, trade analyst

The Tamil Nadu government has capped ticket prices at Rs 190 in Chennai to manage the fan frenzy and ensure public safety. The film is scheduled across 900 screens in Tamil Nadu, with more than 3,500 shows — part of a nationwide total of 8,000 shows.

> **"For the opening weekend, Bala projected Rs 150–180 crore domestically and Rs 250 crore worldwide.

A Seven-Month Delay and a New Cut

Originally slated for January 2026, Jana Nayagan was delayed by certification issues with the Central Board of Film Certification and a major piracy leak. Producer Venkat K Narayana of KVN Productions said the seven-month delay was used to add fresh footage, new songs, and substantial modifications.

The updated version includes references to Vijay's political party, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), and the title card now describes him as "the Honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu." The CBFC ordered roughly 20 seconds of cuts, 10 seconds of replacement footage, and muted religious references before granting certification.

"Vijay is no longer just a star — he's the Chief Minister."**

Strong Overseas Demand from Diaspora Markets

The UK is leading overseas bookings, with distributor Ahimsa Entertainment confirming the film has cleared £1 crore in standalone pre-sales. A key draw for UK audiences: the film will be screened uncut, preserving director H. Vinoth's original vision, according to Sacnilk.

In Canada, exhibitors are taking a phased approach. York Cinemas limited bookings for the first three days to VIP members — fans who had tickets for the film's previously delayed January release — before opening general sales. Australia and Malaysia are also recording rapid sales, suggesting a potential record for an Indian film in those regions.

About 80% of domestic advance bookings have come from southern states, according to Bala, with the Hindi-dubbed version (Jan Neta) drawing minimal traction so far.

"For the opening weekend, Bala projected Rs 150–180 crore domestically and Rs 250 crore worldwide."Vijay is no longer just a star — he's the Chief Minister."

Can It Beat Leo's Rs 606 Crore Record?

Billed as Vijay's 69th and final film, Jana Nayagan faces comparisons to his two biggest grossers: Leo at an estimated Rs 606 crore worldwide and The Greatest of All Time (GOAT) at roughly Rs 458 crore. Produced on a reported budget of Rs 500 crore by KVN Productions, the film features Pooja Hegde, Bobby Deol, Mamitha Baiju, Gautham Vasudev Menon, and Prakash Raj, with music by Anirudh Ravichander.

Tamil Nadu ministers and TVK functionaries have called on party workers to celebrate the release as a "grand festival," with instructions to decorate theaters screening the film in line with party guidelines — turning what might have been a standard Friday release into something closer to a cultural event.
